name: Distributed Energy Resource: Grid-Edge Control, Planning and Operations
description: Introduction to Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and grid-edge concepts; Modeling of DERs i.e. solar PV, energy storage systems, electric vehicles and thermostatically controllable loads and their impact on power flow and grid operations; Power electronic interfaces for DERs including grid-forming and grid-following controls such as droop and virtual inertia; DER coordination and control architectures – centralized, distributed, and local approaches; Distribution system optimization and scheduling with DERs (DistFlow models, inverter constraints, approximations and relaxations); DER Integration standards (volt/var control curves, ride-through capabilities etc), Application of DER flexibility for demand response, NILM-based load disaggregation, peer-to-peer energy trading, voltage and frequency support, and black-start services; Impact of DERs on utility planning (hosting capacity and infrastructure upgrade planning); Co-simulation of transmission–distribution systems to analyze DER interactions with the bulk grid (TSO-DSO interaction); Policy, regulatory, and market frameworks for DER integration (smart metering, retail market mechanisms, and the evolving role of the Distribution System Operator (DSO)).
